newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban bishops welcome pope-Castro meeting.
newsitem.headline: Cuban bishops welcome pope-Castro meeting.

text.p: Cuba's Roman Catholic bishops on Wednesday warmly welcomed the first meeting between President Fidel Castro and Pope John Paul II, and an agreement for the pontiff to visit the island next year.
Cardinal Jaime Ortega said the Cuban church urged the pope's gesture to serve as an example to other countries with links to Cuba, to use dialogue as the best way of seeking solutions to conflicts.

In a statement issued in his capacity as head of the Cuban bishops, Ortega also said the church hoped that recent moves to increase dialogue between authorities and the local church, as well as between Havana and the Vatican, would produce "abundant results for the life of our church and that of all our nation."

The pope accepted Castro's invitation to Cuba, the only Spanish-speaking Latin American country he has not visited, during an historic first meeting with the communist leader at the Vatican on Tuesday.
Ortega said the church greatly appreciated the meeting and was "deeply joyful" that "next year we can welcome to our country Pope John Paul, whose visit we have awaited for so many years."

"We appeal to leaders of those countries whose historic, economic or humanitarian interests link them to Cuba to also look through dialogue for solutions to existing conflicts," he said. "This gesture of the Holy Father invites us to do that."

His call for dialogue was apparently directed partly at the United States, which maintains a longstanding economic embargo against Cuba. The sanctions have been criticised by both the Cuban church and the Vatican.
And, echoing a frequent call by the Cuban bishops, Ortega called on Cuban Catholics both at home and abroad to seek ways of reconciliation.

Reflecting a clear improvement in recent months in church-state relations, Ortega added the church was hopeful that discussions begun in recent months between Cuban authorities and both the local church and the Vatican would continue and would produce results.
